+ ================================================================ +
= "Est.SP"  : shared pool size for estimate                        =
= "Est.LC"  : estimated library cache size                         =
= "Est.PTS" : estimated library cache parse time saved             =
=                                                                  =
= "If rows in the v$shared_pool_advice have the same values        =
= of parse time savings ("Est.PTS") then this indicates            =
= there would be no additional hits on those size ranges           =
= for library cache objects."                                      =
=                                                                  =
= "However, if time saving values increase for larger pool sizes   =
= then this indicates that it may help to increase the shared      =
=  pool size."                                                     =

+ ============================================================== +
= Sebaiknya tidak ada proses wait yang terjadi pada              =
= buffer cache:                                                  =
=    free buffer inspected ~ 0                                   =
=    free buffer waits     ~ 0                                   =
=    buffer busy waits     ~ 0                                   =
=                                                                =
= Jika nilai free buffer waits tinggi, hal ini bisa              =
= disebabkan oleh beberapa hal:                                  =
=   1. I/O system terlalu kecil                                  =
=   2. I/O sedang menunggu resource yg lain (spt latches)        =
=   3. Buffer cache terlalu kecil sehingga DBWn menghabiskan     =
=      banyak waktu untuk memindahkan dirty buffer               =
=   4. Buffer cache terlalu besar sehingg DBWn tidak cukup cepat =
=      memindahkan dirty buffer untuk menyediakan free buffer    =
=      (perkecil buffer cache atau tambahkan jumlah database     =
=      writer DB_WRITER_PROCESSES (0-9)).                        =

**   REDO LOG BUFFER   **
**   ===============   **



**  "WAIT FOR SPACE" pada log buffer (redo buffer allocation  **
**  retries dan redo log space request)                       **
**  ========================================================  **




+ =================================================================== +
= redo buffer allocation retries: berapa kali oracle (users process)  =
= harus mengulangi proses penyimpanan redo entries pada log buffer    =
= sampai berhasil, karena menunggu hingga tersedianya 'space' untuk   =
= menempatkan redo entries.                                           =
=                                                                     =
= Nilai redo log space request sebaiknya ~ 0 (nearest)                =
= Nilai ini mengindikasikan bahwa aktif log file sudah penuh          =
= dan Oracle Server menunggu proses archive log file selesai          =
= sehingga log file space tersedia / dapat digunakan.                 =
+ =================================================================== +



**   REDO BUFFER RETRY RATIO PERCENTAGE (RBRRP)   **
**   ==========================================   **

       ROUND((r.value / e.value) * 100, 2) "RBRRP (%)"

** PGA memory only used in dedicated connection

** aggregate PGA target parameter shows the actual value set for
** PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET. This parameter confirms if automatic PGA
** memory management has been activated -- if it hasn't been,
** then this value will be zero.
** over allocation count tells how much PGA memory has been over-allocated
** cumulatively since the instance was started. If the value returned is
** anything over zero, it is an indication that the size of PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET
** should be increased because it means that Oracle could not honor at least one
** request for additional PGA work areas.

** V$SQL_WORKAREA_HISTOGRAM contains information about how many **
** work areas have been executed with optimal, one-pass, and    **
** multi-pass memory size since the instance was started within **
** a range of work area sizes, defined by LOW_OPTIMAL_SIZE and  **
** HIGH_OPTIMAL_SIZE                                            **
** ============================================================ **

files within a tablespace

Look for a mismatch across disk drives in terms of I/O

Also, examine the Blocks per Read Ratio for heavily accessed
TSs - if this value is significantly above 1 then you may have
full tablescans occurring (with multi-block I/O)

If activity on the files is unbalanced, move files around to balance
the load.  Should see an approximately even set of numbers across files
